> Equipment

Messages.Author: glaswanderer
Messages.Body:
No. Imbued have life not blood, so they cannot pay the 1 blood to activate the Codex.

Prince of Puyallup

Edit:
There's also this relevant part of the rulebook:
>
> 1.6.3. Minion Cards
>
> Minion cards are cards that your vampires and allies (collectively referred to as "minions") play. Unless the card states otherwise, a minion card is burned after a minion plays it.
>
> By default, a minion card in play is controlled by the controller of the minion it is on. If a minion card is just in play and not on another controlled card, then it is, by default, controlled by the Methuselah who played it.
>
> In many cases, a minion card will have a Discipline symbol, a clan symbol and/or a blood cost; in these cases, the card can only be played by a vampire who meets the requirements.
>
> Some allies have the ability to play certain cards "as a vampire." In these cases, the ally is treated as a vampire for all effects generated by the play of the card, including duration effects (like "for the remainder of combat"). The ally's life represents his blood (to pay costs, for example). Any blood he gains or loses as a vampire equates to a gain or loss of life for the ally. For purposes of that card, the ally has a capacity of 1 by default (for use if the card requires an older vampire or a vampire of a given capacity). If the ally gains life in excess of his capacity, it doesn't drain off, and if the effect inflicts aggravated damage on the ally, he burns life as normal. However, if the effect would send the ally to torpor, then he is burned instead. The ally is treated as a vampire only for the effect generated from playing the card. In particular, the ally is not treated as a vampire for effects the card has from being in play (like "the vampire with this card" effects).
>
> Codex of the Edenic Groundskeepers
> Equipment
> [1 Pool]
> Unique equipment.
> This minion gets -2 stealth when bleeding. This minion may bleed as a  action that costs 1 blood; this action gets +3 bleed if the target Methuselah doesn't control a ready untapped minion.
>

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
[quote="Rulebook 6.4.5 - 'Steal Blood'"[/quote]Steal Blood. This effect moves blood counters (or life counters) from the target to the striking minion. [/quote]

Imbued cannot play cards (or use effects) that cost blood. They can steal blood (that transforms to life) or can get stolen life (if via strikes, that would be a "strike: steal blood" effect).

Jennifer's special ability is not worded correctly. It should say "Jennifer can equip with weapons that cost zero or one pool or blood. No cost is paid." With the current card text, she should be able to pay blood costs for any weapon. Golden rule for cards.

Messages.Author: TheLich
Messages.Body:
> TwoRazorReign wrote:
> Yes. But Jennifer's special ability is worded poorly. It suggests that Jennifer can pay blood costs for weapons. I think there is a better way to state Jennifer's special ability.
>
There are cards that would allow her the ability to do so. Because of this they make the ability all encompassing.

Example :

Jennifer who has a Putrescent Servitude and equips a Theoretical Weapon that does not exist yet that happens to cost 2. They could use a Forger's Hammer to have the action end successfully and not unsuccessfully. Any minion can attempt an action with no specific limitations even if they can't afford the cost.

> Putrescent Servitude
> Action
> 1 Blood
> +1 stealth action.
> [thn] Move any mortal or ghoul retainer you control to this vampire, or put this card on a mortal or ghoul ally you control. This ally gains 1 life, and he or she may play cards that require basic Potence as a vampire.
> [THN]  As above, but take any mortal or ghoul retainer or put this card on any mortal or ghoul ally and take control of that ally.
>
> Forger's Hammer
> Action Modifier
> Only usable when this vampire successfully equips with a non-unique melee weapon from your hand.
> [pot] Put this card on the weapon. This weapon inflicts +1 damage each strike.
> [POT] As above, and the cost of this weapon is reduced by 1 blood or 1 pool.
>
There are no rules that say you cannot attempt the action and that it won't technically be successful, but instead that you will not be able to pay the cost and the item will not be acquired as if you had gone to the store without enough money. The action is still a successful action. The cost of the card is only declared was the action is announced, not required to be met.

> All details of the action are declared when the action is announced, including the target(s), the cost, the effects, etc. Any card required for the action is played (face up) at this time. Tap the acting minion (only ready untapped minions can take actions).
>
That, I believe, is the reason for her wording.

Messages.Author: TheLich
Messages.Body:
> Requirements for Playing Cards. Each library card has symbols on the attribute bar (the marble stripe on the left side) for the card type (except for master cards), the clan or Discipline (if any) required to play the card and the cost (if any) of playing that card. Some cards will have other requirements (such as capacity or title) stated in the card text. Only a minion who meets the requirements given on a minion card can play it, while only a Methuselah who controls a ready minion who meets the requirements of a master card can
>
1.6.1.3 does not refer to the cost as a requirement. Quite the contrary, it refers to things which are required to play and isolates separately the cost. However, I'll concede for now that my interpretation may just simply be a rhetoric based problem and drop my feelings there.

Even still 6.2.1 allows my example to work anyway.

> 6.2.1. Announce the Action
>
> All details of the action are declared when the action is announced, including the target(s), the cost, the effects, etc. Any card required for the action is played (face up) at this time. Tap the acting minion (only ready untapped minions can take actions).
>
This is also the rule that allows you to use Sunset Strip, as it is technically a detail of the action.
